name: hard-gate-fires
description: A freight-domain backend role built on the Microsoft stack. The persona's domain preferences all match -- logistics is their strongest positive -- and the role is remote, backend, and IC. The only thing wrong with it is the stack, which is a hard gate. This is the enforced counterpart to the unit tests: it proves a gate still fires, is priced into preference_score, and is reported as a conflict, through the same path RunFitEvaluation uses.
comment: Before the hard-gate change a tripped gate contributed nothing to preference_score, so a JD like this one scored as though the exclusion had never been recorded. The max band below is what makes that regression impossible to reintroduce silently.

other_flags: greenfield rewrite of a legacy load-planning system onto .NET 8

gate_hits.comment: The .NET hard gate is anti_pattern-typed, so it reads required_skills.

preference_score.comment: Capped by hardGateCeiling. A tripped gate must never present as a good preference fit, however well the rest of the role matches.

preference_conflicts.comment: A gate hit is a conflict, not a gap -- the narrative has to be able to name it.
